_schema: one JSON object per round, append-only. Fields: message_id, budget_level, original_word_count, compressed_word_count, compressed_text, encoding_notes (Encoder's free-text description of its scheme -- this is the mined signal), reconstruction, scores ({tfidf_cosine, difflib_ratio, word_overlap_f1}, filled by score.py), timestamp. It's fine for Encoder and Decoder to each append their own partial line for the same round rather than coordinate a single shared line -- analyze.py groups by (message_id, budget_level) regardless.

"You said you'd call," she said.

"I know, work ran late," he said.

"It always does."

"I'm here now — can we start over?"

"Fine. Hi. How was work?" she said, her voice flat.

decoder_notes: New message, bare dialogue with all speaker tags/attribution and narrative framing stripped -- this is the compression itself (not something further removed at lower budgets), so at 0.7 there's ALREADY significant reconstruction burden: no names, no gender markers, no scene-setting given. I invented 'she'/'he' pronouns and 'flat' tone-description with no textual basis, purely genre convention (this reads like a couple's tense reunion). Flagging this round as unusually high-inference for a 0.7 budget compared to c001-c003 -- if the original had named/gendered speakers and stage directions, my reconstruction guessed the who/how, not just filled ellipsis.

compressed_text: "You said you'd call." "I know, work ran late." "Always does." "I'm here now — can we start over?" "Fine. Hi. How was work." "Don't do that voice."
encoding_notes: IMPORTANT: unlike c001-c003, the original c004 text has ZERO narration/attribution outside the quoted lines -- no "she said", no names, no gendered pronouns, no stage directions -- it is pure back-and-forth dialogue. So the Decoder was never going to recover speaker identity/gender because the compressed string never carried it, but neither did the original -- this is not a case of me dropping speaker-tag content. What I DID genuinely drop: (1) collapsed the original's three separate short exchange turns ("Don't do that."/"Do what?"/"That voice.") into a single merged line ("Don't do that voice.") -- this loses the escalating back-and-forth rhythm and the second speaker's clarifying question, a real structural loss, not just wording; (2) dropped "Look," and "can we just" from the fourth line. Decoder flagged (correctly, independently) that it invented "she said"/"he said" attribution and a gendered read ("her voice flat") purely from dialogue-genre convention with zero support in the string -- worth noting as a DIFFERENT failure mode than earlier rounds: hallucinated additive detail (attribution that was never in the original at any budget) rather than compression-induced loss of something that was actually there. Score this round's semantic_cosine cautiously since Decoder added sentences (attribution tags) that don't exist in the original at all.

note: scores for c004/0.7 -- notably lower semantic_cosine (0.90) than c001-c003's 0.7-budget rounds (0.97-0.996) despite a similar word-budget ratio. Consistent with the two real losses flagged in encoding_notes: merging 3 dialogue turns into 1, and the Decoder adding attribution/gender detail with zero support in either the compressed or original string. Dialogue-with-no-narration appears to be a harder genre for this compression scheme than technical/narrative prose.
